classification.difficultyReason: Recognise a quadratic in an absolute value, factor it and interpret the resulting double inequality.

answer.short:
$-1<x<1$ or $3<x<5$.

Put $t=|x-2|$ and factor the quadratic to obtain $1<t<3$.
answer.worked:
Let $t=|x-2|\ge0$, so $(x-2)^2=t^2$.
$$\begin{align*}t^2-4t+3&<0\\(t-1)(t-3)&<0\\1&<t<3\end{align*}$$
Thus $1<|x-2|<3$. The distance of $x$ from $2$ is strictly between $1$ and $3$ units, so
$$-1<x<1\quad\text{or}\quad3<x<5.$$
